name: What is the difference between MDF and solid wood trim?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between MDF and solid wood trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: MDF (medium-density fiberboard) is an engineered wood product ideal for painted finishes, while solid wood is necessary if you plan to stain the trim. MDF offers smooth surfaces without knots and resists seasonal warping, but it is vulnerable to moisture damage if used near standing water. Solid wood provides superior structural durability, holds up better to impact along baseboards, and works well for natural wood grain finishes in rustic or traditional rooms. Choosing between them involves balancing budget against moisture exposure and finish preferences.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF provides a smooth, cost-effective surface for painted trim, while solid wood offers natural grain for staining and holds up better against moisture and physical impacts.
